purpose: Prucalopride is used to treat chronic idiopathic constipation, which means long-lasting constipation that has no clear cause. It helps people who have not found relief with other laxatives. It works to get your bowels moving more regularly so you can have more comfortable, complete bowel movements.
how_it_works: Your digestive system uses a chemical called serotonin to help move things along. Prucalopride attaches to special serotonin receptors in your gut and acts like a signal that tells your intestines to squeeze and push stool through more effectively. Think of it like pressing the 'go' button on your digestive system to get things moving at a healthier pace.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects, especially in the first day or two, include headache, nausea, diarrhea, and stomach pain or cramps. These usually get better as your body adjusts to the medication. You may also feel bloated or have gas.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. This medication is not recommended during pregnancy, so let your doctor know if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is not approved for use in children. If you experience severe stomach pain, stop taking it and contact your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is 2 mg taken by mouth once a day. If you are over 65 years old or have kidney problems, your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 1 mg once daily. You can take it with or without food, and it works best when taken at the same time each day.
